title: Sequences and lists
description: Lists as the primary fixed/dynamic sequence

exercises.title: Create Array
exercises.description: Create an array of 5 ints with values 1,2,3,4,5. Print all elements.
exercises.starter_code:
var arr = new int[5];
// assign 1..5 and print Go-style [1 2 3 4 5]
hints: Initialize via collection expressions or `new[] { ... }`; avoid loops if literals suffice.
Join elements with spaces inside square brackets via `string.Join(" ", arr)`.

exercises.title: Array Iteration
exercises.description: Create array nums = [10, 20, 30}. Use range to Console.WriteLine each element.
hints: `foreach` idiomatically iterates CLR arrays without manual indexes.
Print each scalar on its own line when newline-separated output is required.
exercises.solution:
var nums = new[] { 10, 20, 30 };
foreach (var v in nums) Console.WriteLine(v);

exercises.title: Array Length
exercises.description: Create arr = [1, 2, 3, 4}. Print the length using len(arr).
hints: Length queries use `.Length`, not unmanaged helpers.

exercises.title: Partial Array Initialization
exercises.description: Create an array of 5 ints where only the first two are initialized to 10 and 20. Print the array.
hints: Allocate `new int[size]` then set leading elements—remaining slots default to `0`.
Reuse bracket-join formatting like other stdout array exercises.

exercises.title: 2D Array
exercises.description: Create a 2x2 matrix with values {{1, 2}, {3, 4}}. Print each element on separate lines.
hints: Walk rows/columns with nested `for` loops or `Enumerable.Range`.

exercises.title: Array Sum
exercises.description: Create arr = [10, 20, 30, 40, 50}. Compute the sum of all elements and Console.WriteLine it.
hints: Accumulate inside a tight `foreach`; `checked` arithmetic only if overflows matter.

exercises.title: Array Element Access
exercises.description: Create arr = [100, 200, 300}. Print the first element (index 0) and last element (index 2).
exercises.starter_code:
var arr = new[] { 100, 200, 300 };
// first and last
hints: First element indexes at `0`; last element prefers index-from-end `[ ^1 ]` on modern runtimes.
